**Plan:**

I will evaluate the single story AMSD-2041 ("Live Preview of Content in CMS") for specification agent assignment.

This story has empty acceptance criteria, no dependencies, and no existing spec. It involves live preview functionality across three platforms (GO, UP, MX), which suggests a complex, cross-platform feature with real-time rendering concerns, state synchronization, and potentially security implications (preview URLs, content injection).

Because the acceptance criteria are completely empty, this story needs significant requirements elaboration first (openspec) to define what "live preview" means across GO/UP/MX, then hardening (speckit) for testability, edge cases (e.g., draft vs published state, permission boundaries, preview token expiry), and security review.

I will assign both agents — openspec first, then speckit — with high priority, since this is a complex feature with no existing AC and cross-platform scope.

I will know I'm wrong if the story turns out to be a trivial wrapper or if the PRD indicates it was already hand-curated (in which case I'd skip). I'll check `orchestrations/prd.json` for any existing spec assignments or hand-curation flags before finalizing.

The output must be raw JSON matching the schema with storyId, agents, notes, and priority — I will produce that after confirming the PRD state.

**PLAN:**

This story is **novel** — it requests a new Live Preview capability for Contentstack CMS content that does not exist in the codebase. The existing code shows Contentstack components consuming content via the `useContent` hook (236 callers), but there is no Live Preview connection/real-time update mechanism anywhere visible.

The primary **attachment point** is `useContent` (src/hooks/useContent.ts:5) — every Contentstack component funnels through it to call `getContentByKey`. Live Preview must integrate here to intercept/augment content fetching with preview tokens and real-time update signals. Secondary attachment points are the Contentstack components themselves (ContentstackLink, ContentstackImage, ContentstackTable, etc.) which consume the hook's output — they may need to re-render on live updates.

Since acceptanceCriteria is empty and description is minimal, I'll derive VCs from the description alone (vcSource: "description"), focusing on observable behavior: when a CMS editor modifies content, the previewed page reflects changes in real-time without a full page reload. I'll boundary-stop at Contentstack's external API (can't reach contentstack.io at test time) and frame VCs around what our code sends/receives given mocked responses.

No split needed — 0 ACs, single concern.
